title: Parental Consent vs. Parental Advice for Marriage
description: Understand the legal requirements for parental involvement in Philippine marriages for applicants aged 18 to 25.

requirements.title: Parents' Presence
requirements.description: Parents should ideally appear personally at the Local Civil Registrar.

requirements.title: Valid IDs
requirements.description: Government-issued IDs of both the applicants and the parents/guardians.

requirements.title: Affidavit Form
requirements.description: A sworn statement of consent (for ages 18-20) or advice (for ages 21-24).

requirements.title: Death Certificate
requirements.description: Required if one or both parents are deceased.

checklist.title: Determine Requirement
checklist.description: Check if you need Parental Consent (ages 18-20) or Parental Advice (ages 21-24) based on your age.

checklist.title: Prepare Affidavit
checklist.description: Obtain the correct template and fill out the details for your parents to sign.

checklist.title: Submit Application
checklist.description: Attach the signed and notarized affidavit to your Marriage License application.

content.title: What are Parental Consent and Parental Advice?

blocks.content: Under the **Philippine Family Code**, individuals who wish to marry but have not yet reached the age of 25 are legally required to involve their parents or guardians in the process.

items: **Parental Consent:** Required for applicants aged **18 to 20**.
**Parental Advice:** Required for applicants aged **21 to 24**.

blocks.content:
These documents are commonly used for:
*   Applying for a Marriage License at the Local Civil Registrar
*   Ensuring the legal validity of the marriage (for Consent)
*   Avoiding the mandatory 90-day waiting period (for Advice)

You may need these documents if you are:
- An applicant aged **18, 19, or 20** (Needs **Consent**)
- An applicant aged **21, 22, 23, or 24** (Needs **Advice**)
Following these legal steps ensures your marriage is valid and processed without delays.

blocks.title: Legal Validity (For Consent)
blocks.content: For those under 21, marrying without consent makes the marriage **voidable** (annullable). Obtaining consent secures the marriage's legal standing.

blocks.title: Faster Licensing (For Advice)
blocks.content: For those aged 21–24, if parental advice is not obtained or is unfavorable, the marriage license issuance is **legally suspended for 90 days**. Providing the advice avoids this wait.

blocks.title: Personal Appearance (LCR)
blocks.content: Parents can sign the marriage license application form directly in front of the Local Civil Registrar.

blocks.title: Notarized Affidavit
blocks.content: If parents cannot come to the City Hall, you can bring a notarized **Affidavit of Consent** or **Affidavit of Parental Advice**.
**Pro Tip:** Always double-check for 'Negative Results'. If your record is missing, you must process **Late Registration** at the LCR where the event occurred.

blocks.title: Determine Your Requirement
blocks.content:
Check your age on the day of the marriage license application.
*   18–20 = Consent
*   21–24 = Advice

blocks.title: Talk to Your Parents
blocks.content: Discuss your plans with your parents. Their cooperation is essential for a smooth process.

blocks.title: Prepare the Document
blocks.content: Obtain the template for the **Affidavit of Consent** or **Affidavit of Advice** from the LCR office or a legal forms website.

blocks.title: Signing and Notarization
blocks.content: Have your father, mother, or guardian sign the document. If done outside the LCR office, it must be sworn before a Notary Public.

blocks.title: Submit to the LCR
blocks.content: Attach the signed and notarized affidavit to your Marriage License application.

Applicants may process these documents at:
- **Local Civil Registrar (LCR):** At your City or Municipal Hall.
- **Notary Public Office:** For notarizing the affidavits.

Typical processing timelines include:
*   Preparation: 1 Day
*   LCR Publication: 10 Days (Standard for all licenses)
You can check the status of your marriage license application at the LCR office after the 10-day publication period.

Applicants may experience:
- **Parental Refusal:** If parents refuse consent (under 21), the license **cannot** be issued. If they refuse advice (21–24), the license is delayed by 90 days.
- **Separated Parents:** Generally, the consent/advice of the parent with whom you live or the surviving parent is sufficient.

items: **Forging Signatures:** This is a criminal offense and will render the marriage license (and potentially the marriage) void.
**Wrong Form:** Using a "Consent" form when you are already 22 years old.

blocks.content: Always use the parent's name exactly as it appears on their valid ID.

items: Bring your parents with you to the LCR to avoid the extra step and cost of notarization.
Ensure you have the death certificate ready if one parent is deceased.
If your parents are unavailable, seek a legal guardian's consent/advice.

blocks.content: For the legal templates and specific local requirements for marriage licensing, please refer to:

items: **Local Government Unit (LGU):** Visit the official website or City/Municipal Hall where you are applying for a marriage license.
**PSA Census:** [PSA Official Website](https://psa.gov.ph) (For civil registry guidelines).

blocks.title: What if I am 25 or older?
blocks.content: You no longer need parental consent or advice. You can apply for a marriage license independently.

blocks.title: Can a sibling give consent?
blocks.content: Only if they are your legally appointed guardian. Otherwise, only parents (or surviving parent) can provide the required consent/advice.
